claim_rule: Published constraints are encoded only at the strength supported by the cited source. A candidate signal is not a confirmed planet. Missing astrometry is not evidence.

candidate_2p43d.paper_statement: Further observations and activity modeling are required to confirm or refute the candidate.

rv_detection_summary_well_aligned.note: Vega is viewed nearly pole-on; aligned planets produce weak line-of-sight RV signals.

tess.geometry_note: Pole-on system orientation makes transits intrinsically unlikely for coplanar planets.

gaia_astrometry.reason: The paper explicitly notes that Vega is far beyond the bright limit for standard Gaia processing and does not quantify a reliable Gaia precision for Vega.

H1A_2P43D_RV_CANDIDATE.observed_proxy: P=2.43 d, K~6 m/s, m*sin(i)~20 Earth masses
H1A_2P43D_RV_CANDIDATE.aligned_mass_note: If aligned near Vega's ~6.5 degree spin inclination, 20 Earth masses / sin(6.5 deg) is approximately 177 Earth masses (~0.56 Jupiter masses).
H1A_2P43D_RV_CANDIDATE.next_discriminant: Independent or extended RV series with activity-aware modeling and cadence resolving both 0.676 d rotation and 2.43 d candidate.

H1B_3_TO_5_AU_NEPTUNE_SHEPHERD.reason: NIRCam anchors begin near 7.7 au, while published RV sensitivity for pole-on/well-aligned orbits is substantially weaker; MIRI explicitly notes a possible modest/Neptune-size shepherd near the warm-disk inner edge.
H1B_3_TO_5_AU_NEPTUNE_SHEPHERD.next_discriminant: Joint RV + disk-dynamical injection/recovery targeted at 3-5 au and low/moderate masses.

topa_priority: Reproduce the public TRES time-series ingest and audit the 2.43 d signal without promoting it to a detection.
Keep 3-5 au Neptune-class shepherd as a separate hypothesis from the 2.43 d RV candidate.
Do not encode Gaia as a hard exclusion until a Vega-specific astrometric precision/proper-motion anomaly product with provenance is obtained.
Use new observations to shrink the surviving mass-orbit envelope before adding new hypotheses.
